keyVerseDR: "Whosoever will be greater, shall be your minister." (Mk 10:43)

level1.title: This Week's Catholic Virtue: Leadership
level1.story: Leadership means helping a group reach a goal while helping everyone get along. Leaders serve!
level1.heartIntro: Hang this sheet on the fridge and practice leadership all week. On Saturday, talk together, write what you practiced, and a parent signs.
questions: When did someone in our family lead by serving?
How can we lead others toward Jesus?
actions: Hang this sheet on the fridge
level1.prayer: Jesus, You came to serve. Help me lead others with kindness and help everyone get along. Amen.

activity.title: Daily Action Checklist
activity.intro: Color a star each day, Monday through Saturday. Hang this sheet on the fridge and practice with your family. A parent signs at the end of the week.
items: MON: Help a younger child learn something
TUE: Lead your family in grace before meals
WED: Invite others to play and include all
THU: Encourage a teammate who is trying
FRI: Lead a family clean-up time
SAT: Help plan a fun family activity

level2.title: This Week's Catholic Virtue: Leadership
level2.story: Leadership means guiding a group toward a good goal while helping everyone get along. A Christian leader is a servant leader. Jesus said that whoever wants to be great must serve the others, and He washed His disciples' feet. Good leaders listen, encourage, plan, and make sure no one is left out. You can lead at home, at school, and at church.
level2.heartIntro: Hang this sheet on the fridge and practice leadership all week. On Saturday, talk together, write what you practiced, and a parent signs.
questions: When did someone in our family lead by serving?
How did God help us grow in leadership?
actions: Hang this sheet on the fridge
level2.prayer: Jesus, You came to serve. Help me lead others with kindness and help everyone get along. Amen.

activity.title: Daily Action Checklist
activity.intro: Color a star each day, Monday through Saturday. Hang this sheet on the fridge and practice with your family. A parent signs at the end of the week.
items: MON: Lead a family prayer or Bible reading
TUE: Organize a game where everyone fits in
WED: Help a group solve a problem calmly
THU: Set a good example for younger kids
FRI: Listen to everyone's ideas before deciding
SAT: Serve someone like Jesus washing feet
